requirements.text: Make this look like a comic book photo
requirements.source_phrase: Make this look like a comic book photo

outcomes.description: Transform the image so it has a comic-book visual style while retaining its photographic subject matter.
outcomes.target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book styling?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comic-book visual styling is visibly present; fail if there is no visible comic-book styling; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the overall visual treatment of the supplied image as edited, without requiring a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image retain recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image retains recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance; fail if it does not; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient.
nodes.binding: Assess the edited image for photographic subject matter and appearance. This observation describes the result and does not by itself establish progress toward the requested edit.

nodes.question: Compared with the supplied source, does the edited image show a visible change toward a comic-book-photo appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the comparison shows a visible, attributable change toward comic-book visual treatment while remaining recognizably a photo; fail if there is no visible change toward that treatment, including when the edited image merely retains the source appearance; unknown if the comparison or relevant visual evidence is insufficient.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied source and edited images for progress toward the requested comic-book-photo appearance. Do not count unrelated changes or mere retention of the source scene as progress, and do not require a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image fully look like a comic-book photo?
nodes.criteria: Complete if s1 passes and s3 passes. Partial only if s3 passes and evidence establishes the requested appearance remains incomplete. Absent if s3 fails, establishing no requested progress. Unknown if progress or necessary evidence is unresolved. A pass on s2 alone does not establish progress or completion; ignore unrelated edits.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment rule is not faithful to the rubric’s progress semantics. It makes partial depend on s3 passing, although s3 can fail because the comparison shows no requested progress; that is evidence for absent, not partial. Conversely, s3 passing establishes progress but does not establish that the full requested treatment is incomplete, so partial is not justified without evidence of incompleteness. The readout needs to distinguish complete, evidenced progress with incompleteness, no progress, and unresolved evidence. The support checks otherwise cover styling, photographic appearance, and attributable progress without mandating a technique.

The program adds an unsupported requirement: the image must retain photographic subject matter and appearance. The instruction asks for a “comic book photo,” but does not clearly require preserving the original photographic appearance; the program turns that interpretation into a mandatory completion condition. Also, s3 is nested under s2 and only activates after s2 has an observation, yet its progress test must be usable even when photographic appearance is not retained. This structure can leave progress unresolved when s2 is unknown or fails, despite s3 being the separate evidence needed to distinguish progress from no progress. The fulfillment rule otherwise composes the checks consistently, but these issues prevent faithful coverage of the request.
